subject: Student Substance Abuse Survey and Vaping Awareness
overview: The School Committee reviewed a comprehensive survey on student substance abuse and the rising trend of vaping, approved a revised district field trip policy, and discussed strategies to increase school breakfast participation. The body also received updates on the superintendent search process and the fiscal year 2018 first-quarter financial report.

items.title: Routine business and minutes
items.summary: Approved the minutes from November meetings, bills, fund transfers, and payroll.

items.title: Committee of the Whole Report: November 13
items.summary: Accepted the report covering the North Medford bus capacity, the School Brains data system, and a student concussion incident at an away game in Beverly. Superintendent Belson reported on a dispute with Beverly Public Schools regarding the medical response and official supervision at the game.

items.title: Superintendent Succession Plan Update
items.summary: Accepted the November 27 report regarding the superintendent search, which established a vote to review internal candidates first and explore various search consultants. The committee discussed forming a search committee comprised of teachers, administrators, and parents if an external search is required.

items.title: School Breakfast Program Participation
items.summary: Nutritionist Retta Smith presented data showing that 'breakfast in the classroom' at the Columbus School significantly outperformed traditional cafeteria models. The committee requested that principals evaluate implementing classroom-based breakfast to increase participation and reduce stigma.

items.title: Student Survey on Substance Abuse
items.summary: Team Medford presented results from the 2017 Community Care Survey showing declines in alcohol and prescription drug use but a sharp rise in students 'juuling' or vaping. The committee approved creating student-designed awareness posters and directed the administration to draft specific vaping language for the student handbook.

items.title: Graduation Date and Location
items.summary: Approved the graduation for Medford High School and Medford Vocational Technical High School for June 6, 2018, at the Tufts University Gantcher Center.

items.title: First Quarterly Financial Report
items.summary: Director of Finance and Administration Kirsteen Patterson reported that 42.9% of the general fund operating budget has been spent or encumbered, with major expenditures focusing on security camera upgrades and technology rollouts. The committee noted that district-wide security camera repairs are expected to be completed by mid-December.

items.title: Bilingual Education Legislation
items.summary: The administration reported on the 'LOOK Act,' which provides school districts more flexibility in choosing bilingual education programs over the previous mandatory immersion model. Implementation is deferred until the state Department of Elementary and Secondary Education releases specific guidance and licensure requirements.

items.title: Revised Field Trip Policy
items.summary: Approved a revised field trip policy that includes accessibility statements, updated chaperone CORI requirements, and emergency notification procedures. An amendment was added to require school committee approval for out-of-country travel at least six months in advance unless extenuating circumstances exist.
